newsitem.title: GERMANY: German call money eases as Buba adds funds.
newsitem.headline: German call money eases as Buba adds funds.

text.p: German call money rates slipped to between 3.00 and 3.05 percent on Wednesday from 3.03/3.08 percent on Tuesday after dealers were surprised by the Bundesbank's move to add a net 400 million marks to the money market in this week's repo tender.
Dealers said they had expected the Bundesbank to drain a net two billion marks from the money market.

Commercial banks' effective deposits at the central bank totalled 42.9 billion marks, up from 41.5 billion marks, while the average for the month through Tuesday was 41.0 billion marks, up from 40.9 billion.
